box: XC (local); Postgres local, judgments 151 GB / 18,752,608 est rows

contention.verdict: ISOLATED_ENOUGH for the database, CONTENDED on the box
contention.note: NEW1's coarse walk held the GPU at 99% throughout and its DB client sat idle between batches. A concurrent jest suite ran during the control-plane phase. Every figure below is therefore an UPPER bound, never a production number.

harnessLimit: embedQuery returns null, so the route's dense arm does not run inside the app harness. It is measured separately under denseArmIsolated.

denseArmIsolated.note: Random unit vector at depth 2000. Latency only; no relevance claim.

dominantPhase.name: lexical/sparse ranked retrieval (retrieve.ts:875 df-scored CTE)
dominantPhase.plan: BitmapAnd(judgments_full_text_idx -> 125,093 rows, judgments_court_idx -> 2,276,107 rows) -> Bitmap Heap Scan 9,744 rows over 41,847 heap blocks, Rows Removed by Index Recheck 33,555 -> top-N heapsort on ts_rank
dominantPhase.readAs: The court predicate contributes a 2.27M-entry bitmap (176 ms, 2,610 buffers) purely to intersect a 125k-entry one, and the bitmap goes lossy so the heap recheck re-reads 33,555 rows. Both are index/plan shape, not code.

paragraphFallbackCost.why: retrieve.ts:2534 ts_rank(to_tsvector(paragraph_text)) is bounded by p.judgment_id = ANY(<page ids>) and judgment_paragraphs_judgment_idx drives it. It never exceeded 136 ms of a 940-1148 ms request. Checked rather than assumed.

coldTimeoutNotReproduced.reported: POST /search duration_ms 15243 on a physical Galaxy S24 (RCC bus 1690)
coldTimeoutNotReproduced.arithmetic: 15243 is the 15,000 ms research-pool statement_timeout plus overhead, not a query that merely ran long. retrieve.ts catches 57014 (QUERY_CANCELED) and marks the arm degraded, so such a request still returns 200.
notExcluded: the deployed (Railway) database rather than this box
research-pool queueing: RESEARCH_POOL_MAX is 6, and wait time in the pool is not covered by statement_timeout
coldTimeoutNotReproduced.nextAction: No new instrumentation is needed. route.ts:337 already logs degraded[] beside latencyMs. Pull the production log line for that request id: a non-empty degraded[] names the arm that hit the cap; an empty one means the time went to pool queueing, not to a statement.
